## ✨ Highlights

A security-review release. A review of everything that came since the 2026-10-07 audit - clusters, pairing and rescue, the Controller's warm standby, SSO, the ACME relay and Controller-ordered certificates, state transfer, the connectivity probe, the janusctl plugin - turned up two high and nine medium findings in Janus's own code. All of them are fixed here.

- 🔐 **An HAProxy configuration can no longer reach the node's secrets** ([JANUS-2026-008](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/v2026.11.05/security/fixes/JANUS-2026-008.json)): HAProxy now runs in a mount namespace where STATE's keys are absent, so a configuration an operator applies can't read the node CA key and become admin.
- 🔐 **The Controller only orders the certificates you allow** ([JANUS-2026-009](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/v2026.11.05/security/fixes/JANUS-2026-009.json)): a name policy, set by an admin, says which names each node may be ordered - **ordering is paused until you set it** (see the upgrade notes).
- 🛡️ **Ten more holes closed**: readers no longer see cluster or stick-table secrets, the audit trail can't be forged or flushed, the update relay can't be turned into an SSRF, a DHCP server can't stop HAProxy, a removed cluster member loses its access, a test build can't be signed with the production key, and the janusctl plugin won't auto-run a planted `janusctl`.

Nothing new to configure except the Controller's ACME name policy; every other fix is applied by the update.

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **Let's Encrypt ordered by the Controller is paused until you set a name policy.** If your Controller orders certificates for its nodes (**Let's Encrypt › Ordering for the nodes**), add at least one **name rule** there after updating - a node is ordered a name only if a rule whose labels match it covers the name's suffix. If you use a CA other than Let's Encrypt, add it to the allowed directories. Until a rule covers a node's names, its ordering stops (its existing certificates keep being served). This is [JANUS-2026-009](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/v2026.11.05/security/fixes/JANUS-2026-009.json)'s fix: without it, an operator of one node could have the Controller order a wildcard of your zone or another node's name.
- **A cluster whose member you removed before updating**: re-apply it once, so every remaining member has the current composition - that is what now refuses a removed member's certificate ([JANUS-2026-017](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/v2026.11.05/security/fixes/JANUS-2026-017.json)).
- **Update the janusctl Claude Code plugin** (`/plugin`) for [JANUS-2026-012](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/v2026.11.05/security/fixes/JANUS-2026-012.json).

## 🔒 Security

Janus's own code, found by the 2026-11-05 security review (the report ships with the fixes it is complete for):

- **Janus itself** (nodes), its own code:
  - 🟠 high [JANUS-2026-008](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/v2026.11.05/security/fixes/JANUS-2026-008.json) - An HAProxy configuration could read the node's private keys and credentials, turning an operator into an admin
  - 🟡 medium [JANUS-2026-010](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/v2026.11.05/security/fixes/JANUS-2026-010.json) - An operator could evade the HAProxy global-section policy with quotes or a conditional block
  - 🟡 medium [JANUS-2026-011](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/v2026.11.05/security/fixes/JANUS-2026-011.json) - A DHCP server could stop a node's HAProxy or inject a nameserver with a crafted host name or domain
  - 🟡 medium [JANUS-2026-016](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/v2026.11.05/security/fixes/JANUS-2026-016.json) - A node reader could read stick-table keys, including clients' session tokens
  - 🟡 medium [JANUS-2026-017](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/v2026.11.05/security/fixes/JANUS-2026-017.json) - A cluster member removed from the cluster kept its member access
  - 🟡 medium [JANUS-2026-018](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/v2026.11.05/security/fixes/JANUS-2026-018.json) - A test image build could be signed with the production Secure Boot key
- **Janus Controller itself** (the Controller), its own code:
  - 🟠 high [JANUS-2026-009](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/v2026.11.05/security/fixes/JANUS-2026-009.json) - A node operator could make the Controller order a certificate for any name, wildcards included
  - 🟡 medium [JANUS-2026-013](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/v2026.11.05/security/fixes/JANUS-2026-013.json) - A Controller reader could read a cluster's haproxy.cfg, VRRP/BGP and per-member secrets
  - 🟡 medium [JANUS-2026-014](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/v2026.11.05/security/fixes/JANUS-2026-014.json) - A node operator could make the Controller fetch an arbitrary URL through the update relay
  - 🟡 medium [JANUS-2026-015](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/v2026.11.05/security/fixes/JANUS-2026-015.json) - An unauthenticated client could forge the Controller's log lines and flush its audit trail
- **janusctl and the Terraform provider itself** (janusctl and the Terraform provider), its own code:
  - 🟡 medium [JANUS-2026-012](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/v2026.11.05/security/fixes/JANUS-2026-012.json) - The janusctl Claude Code plugin auto-allowed any executable named janusctl

## 🖥️ Controller

- **Only the names you allow are ordered** ([JANUS-2026-009](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/v2026.11.05/security/fixes/JANUS-2026-009.json)): the **Let's Encrypt › Ordering for the nodes** tab gains a **Policy** - name rules by labels, and the allowed CA directories. See the upgrade notes.
- **Readers no longer see a cluster's secrets** ([JANUS-2026-013](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/v2026.11.05/security/fixes/JANUS-2026-013.json)): a version's haproxy.cfg is masked and the VRRP/BGP templates and per-member variables are left out, as a node masks them for readers.
- **The update relay checks you may upgrade the node before it fetches** ([JANUS-2026-014](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/v2026.11.05/security/fixes/JANUS-2026-014.json)) and follows a redirect only to the same host.
- **The audit trail can't be forged or flushed** ([JANUS-2026-015](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/v2026.11.05/security/fixes/JANUS-2026-015.json)): log lines quote their fields, the recorded path is capped, and unauthenticated entries are rate-limited per address.

## 🧰 Nodes

- **HAProxy runs with STATE's secrets out of reach** ([JANUS-2026-008](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/v2026.11.05/security/fixes/JANUS-2026-008.json)): a mount namespace for the serving process and every `haproxy -c`.
- **The global-section check can't be dodged** ([JANUS-2026-010](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/v2026.11.05/security/fixes/JANUS-2026-010.json)): it tokenizes a line the way HAProxy does and refuses the `.if/.elif/.else/.endif` conditionals.
- **A DHCP server's host name and domain are validated** ([JANUS-2026-011](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/v2026.11.05/security/fixes/JANUS-2026-011.json)) before they reach the hostname, the peers file or resolv.conf.
- **Stick-table keys are masked for readers** ([JANUS-2026-016](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/v2026.11.05/security/fixes/JANUS-2026-016.json)) when they can be a client's cookie or credential.
- **A removed cluster member loses its access** ([JANUS-2026-017](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/v2026.11.05/security/fixes/JANUS-2026-017.json)).

## 🔧 Build and tooling

- **A test image build is signed with a throwaway key**, never the production Secure Boot key ([JANUS-2026-018](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/v2026.11.05/security/fixes/JANUS-2026-018.json)).
- **The janusctl plugin auto-allows only a real janusctl** ([JANUS-2026-012](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/v2026.11.05/security/fixes/JANUS-2026-012.json)), not a `./janusctl` from the working tree.
